director.title: Director
director.subtitle: Steer the novel while it is written: the webnovel style profile, your standing notes, and 'redo chapter N with this note'. Everything here reaches the planner and the drafter; nothing is advisory.
director.pendingNote: The novel project does not exist yet. Edits made now are saved on the job and applied the moment the project is created, before the first chapter is planned.
director.runningNote: The job is running. Style and directive edits take effect from the next chapter; pause the job to redo a chapter.

derived.author: author-edited
derived.detected: detected from the reference and your brief

style.subgenreHint: Switching the template re-seeds the progression engine (tiers, rewards, world hooks) for the new subgenre; your other edits are kept.
style.saved: Style saved. The next chapter compiles against it.

directives.hint: Standing notes in your own words. 'Novel' notes reach every planning and drafting prompt; arc and chapter notes reach only the chapters in range. Chapter numbers already drafted are listed on each note.
directives.empty: No directives yet. The engine writes from the style profile and the Story Charter alone.
directives.textPlaceholder: e.g. The protagonist never begs. Rank-ups are earned on the page, never off-screen.

problems.chapter_from: Chapter and arc notes need a starting chapter.
problems.chapter_to: The arc must end at or after its first chapter.
problems.beyond_count: That chapter is beyond the novel's chapter count.

redo.hint: Rewind the canon to chapter N−1, discard chapters N and later, and regenerate them under your note. Chapters below N are untouched. The blueprint window from N is re-planned first so the note can change what happens, not only how it is written.
redo.note: Author's note for the regenerated chapter
redo.notePlaceholder: e.g. Chapter 14 must open at the assessor's desk; the rank-up happens in public.
redo.confirmBody: Chapter texts {list} are snapshotted then discarded; canon and ledgers rewind to chapter {prev}. This cannot be undone from the UI.
redo.done: Rewound to chapter {prev}. Chapter {n} regenerates next.
redo.needsPause: Pause the job first; a running job cannot be rewound safely.
redo.needsChapters: No committed chapter to redo yet.
redo.needsStage: Chapters can be redone once drafting has started.

quality.hint: Deterministic conformance per committed chapter: how much the prose reads like the target webnovel style, before and after the craft passes.
